title: Mechanisms of enhanced or impaired DNA target selectivity driven by protein dimerization.
authors: Sang, Mankun; Au, Gabriel; Johnson, Margaret E
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过质量作用动力学模型和空间随机模拟研究二聚化对蛋白-DNA结合靶标选择性的影响，虽非典型TF-DNA体系，但聚焦蛋白-DNA互作动态机制且方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: Successful DNA transcription demands coordination between proteins that bind DNA while simultaneously binding to one another to form dimers or higher-order complexes. For proteins with numerous DNA targets throughout the genome, measurements that report on their dwell time or occupancy thus represent a convolution over a population interacting with specific DNA, nonspecific DNA, or protein partners on DNA. Dimerization is known to add contacts that can help a single protein to stably bind DNA. However, we show here that dimerization can also impair measured dwell times and occupancy on target sequences because the population redistributes across DNA. We combine mass-action kinetic models of pairwise reversible reactions between proteins and DNA with theory and spatial stochastic simulations to isolate the role of dimerization on observed DNA dwell times, occupancy, and spatial distribution of proteins on DNA. Three key themes emerge: (i) Protein-protein interactions, in addition to protein-DNA interactions, can localize a protein to DNA, and relative binding rates can thus widely tune dwell times. (ii) Dimensional reduction achieved through nonspecific binding and subsequent 1D diffusion controls the order-of-magnitude of enhancements despite nucleosome barriers. (iii) Dimerization enhances selectivity for locally clustered targets and often impairs binding to widely-spaced targets by sequestration. Compared with ChIP-seq data, our model explains how the distribution of the essential GAF protein throughout the genome is highly selective for clustered targets due to protein interactions. This model framework predicts when even weak dimerization can redistribute and stabilize proteins on DNA as a necessary part of transcription.
abstract_zh: 成功的DNA转录需要DNA结合蛋白之间的协调，这些蛋白在结合DNA的同时彼此结合形成二聚体或高阶复合物。对于基因组中拥有众多DNA靶标的蛋白质，测量其停留时间或占据率的实验，因此代表了对与特异性DNA、非特异性DNA或DNA上蛋白伙伴相互作用的群体的卷积。已知二聚化能增加接触点，有助于单个蛋白质稳定结合DNA。然而，我们在此表明，二聚化也可能损害靶序列上的测量停留时间和占据率，因为群体在DNA上重新分布。我们将蛋白质与DNA之间成对可逆反应的质量作用动力学模型与理论和空间随机模拟相结合，以分离二聚化对观察到的DNA停留时间、占据率及蛋白质在DNA上空间分布的作用。三个关键主题浮现：（i）蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用，除蛋白质-DNA相互作用外，可将蛋白质定位到DNA上，因此相对结合速率可广泛调节停留时间。（ii）通过非特异性结合及随后的1D扩散实现的维度降低，控制增强的数量级，尽管存在核小体屏障。（iii）二聚化增强对局部聚集靶标的选择性，并常通过隔离损害对广泛间隔靶标的结合。与ChIP-seq数据相比，我们的模型解释了必需GAF蛋白在整个基因组中的分布如何因蛋白质相互作用而对聚集靶标高度选择。该模型框架预测，即使弱二聚化也能作为转录的必要部分，重新分布并稳定DNA上的蛋白质。
